captions.text: Tokyo took a tea break. And
left America with an unfunded bar
tab. The Fed hasn't moved, but
your borrowing costs climbed
anyway. Three men in blue ties
blame the deficit, the Fed, or
the vibes at Jackson Hole. On
YouTube, it's sixty-three stick
figures. Here's what nobody on
that panel is watching: our
biggest lender. The Treasury's
table shows Japan holds over a
trillion dollars of our debt, and
it's been selling since February.
I ran risk at JPMorgan; when
your biggest customer walks, the
auction sets your price. The
opponent isn't the Fed; it's a
Japanese balance sheet. Two
numbers show where the money went:
a Treasury page, and your phone.
By the end you'll read both
numbers yourself.
Since February, Japan has sold a
hundred and twenty-two billion
dollars of it, a tenth of
the pile. The Treasury prints the
new total monthly, and that print
is your first number. Tokyo has
pledged ten trillion yen to chips,
and if that works, it beats
our bonds. And here's what nobody
says: the money went home, and
the tab stayed here. So, the
second number: it's on your phone.
Pull up Meta and find its
price-to-earnings multiple: that's
the share of the price that's
profit not yet earned, and a
higher yield discounts it. The Fed
still hasn't moved. Tokyo is still
on its tea break. And that
unfunded bar tab is still ours.
